reasons: internal/app/finding_ops.go:83 "Three paths write data->>'assignee' and only two used to check it" is false, and it is the premise the whole rule is documented on. There are four writers: saveDomain/validateResource (domain.go:468), validateFindingBulk (finding_bulk.go:60), the ITSM sync (automation_workflows_tickets.go:50-62, workflowText(s,200)+TrimSpace), and the generic scanner import at imports.go:102, which puts `assignee` through str() and is written straight to the row by ingestFindings (imports.go:304/INSERT, imports.go:297/UPDATE) without ever calling validateResource. I read all four. Fix the count and name the import path explicitly, and state in the comment whether it is deliberately left out of the rule or is a follow-up — do not silently leave it as "two of three checked".

internal/app/finding_ops.go:83 and commit 1e2cd22 ("apply one assignee rule to every path that stores a finding assignee") overclaim coverage, and the uncovered fourth path interacts with the new carve-out: the "equal to old -> skip" exemption at finding_ops.go:112 is justified in the comment as an accommodation for values that "predate the rule", but imports.go:102 keeps minting out-of-rule assignees after this ships (no byte limit, no control-character check), and every one of those is then permanently exempt on each later PUT. So the rule is not closed and the comment/commit say it is. Reword the commit message (or add a corrective commit) to the coverage actually delivered, and record the import gap.

internal/app/finding_ops.go:91-92 "the detail view and the recipient match in notification_automation_recipients.go read it as assigned" is wrong about the recipient match. notification_automation_recipients.go:78 compares the raw string against u.ID and u.Username, so a whitespace-only assignee matches no user and behaves as unassigned - the same direction as the queue SQL, not the opposite. Only the detail view disagrees (web/src/triage.tsx:425, `item.assignee || "미지정"`, and "   " is truthy). The conclusion ("two different findings to two counters") survives on the detail view alone; drop the recipient-match clause so the justification is not restated in release notes as a three-way split.
notes: The code itself is correct and I proved both regression tests genuinely red against the pre-change code, not just green: removing the three-line hook at domain.go:468 makes TestFindingAssigneeIsWiredIntoResourceValidation fail with the pre-change message, and reverting sameJSONValue to `==` makes TestFindingAssigneeToleratesUncomparableStoredValues panic with "comparing uncomparable type map[string]interface {}" at finding_ops.go:112. Both edits restored; `git status --short` clean afterwards. gofmt (4 changed files) clean, go vet ./internal/app clean, go build ./cmd/hunter OK, go test -count=1 ./internal/app OK, node scripts/verify-pentagi.mjs verified 312 pinned files. Only the three comment/commit-message claims above need changing; the implementation does not.

No behavioral regression found. Every input the bulk path rejected before is still rejected with 400 (only `assignee: null` changed message, from the shared sentence to "조치 담당자에는 이름 또는 빈 문자열을 입력하세요", and that case is pinned by a test). The trim write-back only fires on a value that actually differs from the stored one, so there is no data migration and no mass rewrite; revert is two commits with no external state. ITSM conflict detection is unaffected because automation_workflows_tickets.go:62 already TrimSpaces what it stores, so a trimmed local value was already a conflict before this change.

openapi.json maxLength:200 counts code points while the server counts bytes, so a 100-character Korean name passes the schema and gets a 400 - x-max-bytes:200 is there and this matches the existing FindingBulkPatch declaration, so it is consistent rather than new. The two touched schemas (Finding, FindingUpdate) are also response shapes, so a legacy >200-byte assignee now violates the schema it is returned under; this is documentation-only because openapi.json is never used to validate (internal/app/openapi.go just embeds and serves it, and web/src only links to /api/openapi.json - no maxLength is read in web/src/resources.tsx or resource-form-state.ts). No webassets rebuild needed: zero web changes.

No security or legal blocking finding, so `blocking` is empty. No protected file touched (no auth, oidc, session, or migration change; initFindingOps' CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS is untouched by the diff). No new route, no new public path, no authorization widening - the whole change is reachable only with findings:write. No new dependency, no cryptography, no hand-rolled comparison of a secret. The error sentence is fixed and never quotes the submitted name back (a test asserts that), and a.audit at domain.go:383 still passes only name/title, so the assignee - which is personal data - is not newly written to audit details, logs, or error bodies. No new collection, retention, or sharing of personal data; the change only narrows what can be stored.
